prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1996 implements a proper Accept-header/media-range parser (acceptsMediaType) that splits on commas, trims whitespace, lowercases, honors `q=0` as an explicit rejection, and can match wildcard media ranges (e.g. `*/*`, `type/*`). #2046 instead uses a bare `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` substring check, which does not respect `q=0` (a client explicitly excluding JSON would still be accepted) and does not support wildcard Accept values, and is also more prone to false-positive substring matches on unrelated media types. #1996's diff is self-contained in a dedicated helper function, making the accept-header logic easier to unit test and reuse than #2046's inline conditional rewrite.

clusters.pick_reason: #1996 implements a proper Accept-header/media-range parser (acceptsMediaType) that splits on commas, trims whitespace, lowercases, honors `q=0` as an explicit rejection, and can match wildcard media ranges (e.g. `*/*`, `type/*`). #2046 instead uses a bare `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` substring check, which does not respect `q=0` (a client explicitly excluding JSON would still be accepted) and does not support wildcard Accept values, and is also more prone to false-positive substring matches on unrelated media types. #1996's diff is self-contained in a dedicated helper function, making the accept-header logic easier to unit test and reuse than #2046's inline conditional rewrite.

clusters.pick_reason: 2215 makes the same trailing-slash normalization change as 2214, but also updates shouldAttemptFallback's root-path check (from comparing against '/' to comparing against '') so it stays consistent with paths that now normalize to an empty string instead of '/'. Without that follow-on fix (as in 2214), root-like multi-slash paths that normalize to '' would no longer match the '/' sentinel, causing an extra redundant fallback discovery request. 2215 also factors the logic into a shared normalizeDiscoveryPath() helper instead of duplicating the strip in two separate places.

members.author: raashish1601

Both PRs replace this with a regex-based `.replace(/\/+$/, '')` strip on the exact same lines of buildWellKnownPath.

clusters.pick_reason: #1996 implements a proper Accept-header/media-range parser (acceptsMediaType) that splits on commas, trims whitespace, lowercases, honors `q=0` as an explicit rejection, and can match wildcard media ranges (e.g. `*/*`, `type/*`). #2046 instead uses a bare `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` substring check, which does not respect `q=0` (a client explicitly excluding JSON would still be accepted) and does not support wildcard Accept values, and is also more prone to false-positive substring matches on unrelated media types. #1996's diff is self-contained in a dedicated helper function, making the accept-header logic easier to unit test and reuse than #2046's inline conditional rewrite.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add the same src/index.ts + test/index.test.ts pair for the same missing root-entry problem, but they take conflicting export strategies that can't both be merged. #2030's index.ts does `export * from './client/index.js'` and `export * from './server/index.js'` in addition to types/inMemory; if client and server modules share any identically-named exports, that combination fails to type-check with TS2308 (duplicate identifier), which is exactly the collision #2523 documents in its own file comments and deliberately avoids by keeping Client/Server on their `./client`/`./server` subpaths and only re-exporting types + inMemory from root. #2523 also ships a changeset (`.changeset/fix-root-export-missing-index.md`) declaring the patch bump, which #2030's diff lacks, and its code comments cite the originating issue (#2273) for traceability. Recommend closing #2030 in favor of #2523's narrower, collision-safe export surface.

clusters.pick_reason: 2215 makes the same trailing-slash normalization change as 2214, but also updates shouldAttemptFallback's root-path check (from comparing against '/' to comparing against '') so it stays consistent with paths that now normalize to an empty string instead of '/'. Without that follow-on fix (as in 2214), root-like multi-slash paths that normalize to '' would no longer match the '/' sentinel, causing an extra redundant fallback discovery request. 2215 also factors the logic into a shared normalizeDiscoveryPath() helper instead of duplicating the strip in two separate places.

members.title: chore(client): normalize trailing slashes in discovery paths
members.author: raashish1601
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2215: Both fix the same root cause: buildWellKnownPath's trailing-slash stripping only removed a single trailing slash via `pathname.endsWith('/') ? pathname.slice(0,-1) : pathname`, leaving malformed double-slash well-known paths when the input has multiple trailing slashes. Both PRs replace this with a regex-based `.replace(/\/+$/, '')` strip on the exact same lines of buildWellKnownPath.
